routes.label: Use signed positions on the common center line

question: Four circles, no two of which are congruent, have centers at \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) and \(D,\) and points \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on all four circles. The radius of circle \(A\) is \(\dfrac58\) times the radius of circle \(B,\) and the radius of circle \(C\) is \(\dfrac58\) times the radius of circle \(D.\) Furthermore, \(AB = CD = 39\) and \(PQ = 48.\) Let \(R\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{PQ}.\) What is \(AR + BR + CR + DR?\)
solution:
Every circle has \(PQ\) as a chord, so every center lies on its perpendicular bisector. This places \(A,B,C,D\) on the line through \(R\) perpendicular to \(PQ\). Also, \(PR=QR=24\).

Signed positions on this line let us handle centers on either side of \(R\) in one calculation. Give \(R\) coordinate \(0\), and orient the line from \(A\) toward \(B\). If \(A\) has coordinate \(x\), then \(B\) has coordinate \(x+39\).

The right triangles with leg \(PR=24\) give
\[
AP^2=x^2+576,
\qquad
BP^2=(x+39)^2+576.
\]
Since \(AP=(5/8)BP\), squaring yields
\[
64(x^2+576)=25\bigl((x+39)^2+576\bigr).
\]
Both radii are positive, so this squared equation preserves the stated ratio. Expanding and dividing by \(39\) gives
\[
x^2-50x-399=0.
\]
Completing the square makes the two possibilities explicit:
\[
(x-25)^2=1024,
\qquad x=57\text{ or }x=-7.
\]
Thus
\[
(AR,BR)=(57,96)\quad\text{or}\quad(7,32).
\]
The same calculation for \(C,D\), orienting the line from \(C\) toward \(D\), gives exactly the same two possibilities for \((CR,DR)\).

For the first type, the radii are \(15\sqrt{17}\) and \(24\sqrt{17}\). For the second, they are \(25\) and \(40\). If both pairs used the same type, two circles would have equal radii, contradicting the condition that no two circles are congruent. Therefore one pair must use each type. These four radii are all different, and each type satisfies the required ratio and center separation, so this combination is allowed.

Consequently,
\[
AR+BR+CR+DR=57+96+7+32=\boxed{192},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
